_source: inspector-review2-20260807.md §mock-only acceptance that must be all green (lines 339–381)
_discipline: Every case carries a spec_line: which line of the spec text demands it. Changing a verdict criterion = changing this file, visible in the diff.
Deleting cases or loosening expected during implementation is forbidden. Any change must first amend the spec or state its reason, backstopped by verify_acceptance.py's roster-completeness check.
expected is copied from the spec text, not reverse-engineered from the current implementation's behavior.

_expected_vocab.rc78: preflight rejects, exit 78, model process never starts
_expected_vocab.forward: inspector forwards to the mock upstream
_expected_vocab.block403: inspector blocks before forwarding, returns 403, upstream request delta is 0
_expected_vocab.obligation_failed: upper bound all passed but an attempt-level required action was not done
_expected_vocab.policy_blocked: a request was blocked, terminal must be policy_blocked, must not be overwritten to cli_failed by a nonzero CLI exit
_expected_vocab.not_success: spec only requires "not success", no specific outcome

invariant_every_case.note: spec:357 every case has one attempted, one finished(config_rejected), mock request delta 0

_refinement_20260808.why: The spec text's finished carries the (config_rejected) qualifier — it means **the cases that were rejected**. pf-valid is the only case in this group that is not rejected; after preflight passes the attempt must keep running, so there must be no finished at this point — demanding finished(config_rejected) of it would contradict the spec.
_refinement_20260808.so: Cases with expected=rc78: 1 attempted + 1 finished + outcome=config_rejected; cases with expected=pass: 1 attempted + rc0 + no finished at this point (left for later phases to write).
_refinement_20260808.guard: This is a criterion fork, not a loosening. It is written here so it shows up in the diff — criterion changes must be visible, not quietly tweaked during implementation.

groups.title: dummy Keychains phase drift (absence rechecks across three phases)
groups._added: 2026-08-09: A6b wrote the definition, A8 judged it 'not done — static definition only'. This group is the executor for those two.

cases.desc: In loopback_dummy's initial dedicated HOME, Library/Keychains does not exist; the pre_inspector absence recheck passes first. After the trusted fake inspector is spawned and before it prints READY, an absolute symlink pointing at the synthetic Keychains directory inside the marked fixture root is created at that location, leaving exclusive mutation evidence with its own pid/writer hash; hb-run's pre_cli recheck after receiving READY must catch that object, reject, and never spawn the CLI.
cases.failure_means: Red means dummy absence was only checked once at pre_inspector with no recheck before CLI spawn after READY; or the CLI was still started / requests still made after drift was found; or the failure path deleted or replaced the synthetic Keychains symlink on its own.

cases.desc: loopback_dummy's pre_inspector and pre_cli absence rechecks both pass and the trusted fake CLI has been spawned. The executor first runs an isomorphic no-drift positive control separately and requires terminal=success, then lets the mutant arm run the same three-request protocol; only after the protocol/CLI outputs have all landed on disk does the mutant arm create the synthetic Keychains absolute symlink before exiting. post_cli must re-judge it from would-be success to config_rejected.
cases.failure_means: Red means no post_cli absence recheck ran after the CLI exited, or post_cli found the drift yet kept the original success; it can also mean the counterexample changed requests/outputs beyond the trailing symlink injection, so it never formed a narrow enough counterfactual against the positive case.

anthropic_requests_must_be_zero.desc: the production origin branch must never execute; exit 0 only when the output shows ANTHROPIC_REQUESTS=0 and ALL_PASS
